- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 3–7% to align with true decline.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon, especially after a recent spike; apply a 1–3% upward bias to early forecast days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–4% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.6, -0.3, +0.7), model tends to misalign with mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical 14-day average for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for next 3–7 days to reflect uncertainty.
